summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY. I drive performance analysis and optimization end to end: benchmarking MPI workloads to a 30x speedup, isolating load imbalance that cost up to 65% throughput, and rewriting CUDA C++ kernels for a 35% speedup. Backed by real-time programming on ARM Cortex-M4 (bare-metal C, interrupts, FreeRTOS) and TensorRT tuning on NVIDIA Jetson under Linux.

experience.title: Research Intern (Capstone)
bullets: Designed a custom wavelet bank (alpha-blended sym6+bior3.5) combined with optimized homography stitching and concurrency, raising PSNR from 65 to 86 over the baseline pipeline.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Built a Python GUI (PyQt, Matplotlib) for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization; ran data analysis and technical documentation in JupyterHub with GitLab version control.

projects.name: Parallel Ray Tracer with MPI Task Scheduling
bullets: Benchmarked four parallel work distribution strategies (static strip, block, cyclic, dynamic task queue) rendering 5000x5000 scenes over MPI, achieving up to 30x speedup across 55 processes; dynamic queue won under unpredictable workloads.

projects.name: MPI Hodgkin-Huxley Neuron Simulation
bullets: Distributed dendrite computations across MPI workers on a SLURM-managed cluster for up to 10.49x speedup with 12 processes; identified load imbalance as a performance bottleneck causing up to 65% degradation.

projects.name: CUDA Kernel Optimization for VGG16 Inference
bullets: Wrote custom CUDA C++ conv kernels with memory coalescing, constant memory and preallocated buffers: 49.2ms vs 73.3ms uncoalesced and 77.5ms CPU, a ~35% speedup at identical accuracy.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built ARM Cortex-M4 firmware in bare-metal C at 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM with a deterministic 1 Hz real-time update rate.
Wrote a low-level I2C device driver and programmed GPIO, TIM2 and ADC1 directly, with timer-triggered ADC scan conversions and interrupt-driven sample capture.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination on an STM32 (ARM Cortex-M4), with interrupt-driven UART commands from a YOLOv8 tracker on NVIDIA Jetson driving multi-servo PWM control.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Optimized YOLO with TensorRT on NVIDIA Jetson for a 5.2x speedup (56.7 to 10.9 ms, 17.6 to 92 FPS vs eager PyTorch), reaching 100% pick reliability over 10 trials.
Deployed the Jetson-side bridge as a Linux systemd service with auto-restart, non-root isolation and static IP networking.
